references.title: Stanford CS221, Ken Liu, Introduction to Language Models, November 17, 2025, pinned official slide deck
references.supports: representation, chain rule, n-grams, shifted targets, task conditioning, architecture, pre/post-training, tokenization, systems, and dated ecosystem overview. The chapter corrects illustrative ID/normalization and unit discrepancies; its program is original.

references.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
references.supports: , retained v3 PDF pages 1–2 and 8: reported 405B/15.6T/3.8e25 scale, post-training recipe, measured iso-compute fits versus extrapolation. These are reported historical values.

references.title: Qwen3 Technical Report
references.supports: , PDF pages 1, 3–4: 36T training tokens, byte-level tokenizer identification, diverse/synthetic data and stages. Token-to-word/byte conversions here are separate assumptions.

references.title: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need
references.supports: , PDF pages 3–5, §§3.1–3.4: shifted targets, causal masking, projected scaled dot-product attention, positionwise feed-forward sharing. Cache induction and numerical constructions are original extensions.

references.title: Devlin et al., BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
references.supports: , PDF page 4, §3.1: masked-position objective and its replacement scheme, distinct from autoregressive generation.

references.title: Radford et al., Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
references.supports: , 2019 report PDF pages 1–2, §2: task/input/output conditioning and bounded task-transfer experiments.

references.title: Brown et al., Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
references.supports: , PDF pages 1, 3, 6–7: definition and evaluation distinction between task fine-tuning and fixed-parameter context demonstrations; reported successes do not certify all tasks.

references.title: Kaplan et al., Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
references.supports: , PDF pages 1–2: empirical loss-scaling scope. The chapter makes no unrestricted extrapolation or current leaderboard claim.

references.title: Hoffmann et al., Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
references.supports: , retained v1 PDF pages 1–2 and 5–6: fixed-compute tradeoff, measured curves, and proposed parametric loss form. The allocation derivation and unit-coefficient example are original conditional mathematics.

references.title: Ouyang et al., Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
references.supports: , PDF pages 1–9, especially Figure 2 and §3.5: SFT/comparison/reward/PPO pipeline, labeler-population limits, logistic comparison fitting, reference log-ratio penalty, and residual mistakes. The finite tilt is an original idealized optimization, not the reported PPO implementation.

references.title: Sennrich, Haddow, and Birch, Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
references.supports: , PDF pages 3–4, §3.2, Algorithm 1, Figure 1, and footnote 3: character-based within-word BPE and coverage qualification. The byte program is a separate declared construction.

references.title: Dao et al., FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
references.supports: , PDF pages 1–4, §§2–3: memory hierarchy, arithmetic intensity, tiling and recomputation. No published speedup is transferred to this CPU program.
